evidence.claim: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's authoritarian government regularly targeted perceived government critics and political opponents and exerted strong control over the media and judiciary in the long run-up to the 2023 elections.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Turkey
evidence.excerpt: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's authoritarian government regularly targeted perceived government critics and political opponents and exerted strong control over the media and judiciary in the long run-up to the 2023 elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary HRW country chapter with direct 2022-summary language and specific examples in the surrounding section.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 coverage summarized in a 2023 country chapter.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's government and political environment.
contrary_evidence: The chapter still reflects a mixed domestic picture rather than a pure mass-violence setting.

evidence.claim: Domestic and international rights groups reported that some police officers, prison authorities, and military and intelligence units employed torture or other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, and the government did not always observe protections against arbitrary arrest and detention.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Turkey
evidence.excerpt: Domestic and international rights groups reported that some police officers, prison authorities, and military and intelligence units employed torture or other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, and the government did not always observe protections against arbitrary arrest and detention.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. government annual report with detailed 2022 country findings and specific line-level allegations summarized from multiple sources.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's government because it describes state security forces and detention practices under his executive system.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes civilian authorities maintained effective control over security forces, so the issue is impunity and abuse rather than outright loss of control.

evidence.claim: Police used tear gas, pepper spray, and detentions to disperse the March 8 women's march and repeatedly prevented the Saturday Mothers from assembling, including detaining participants during the 900th-week vigil.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Turkey
evidence.excerpt: Police used tear gas, pepper spray, and detentions to disperse the March 8 women's march and repeatedly prevented the Saturday Mothers from assembling, including detaining participants during the 900th-week vigil.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same official report, but a materially distinct claim on protest treatment and repeated suppression of peaceful assembly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Erdoğan government because it reflects state policing and administrative restrictions on peaceful assembly.
contrary_evidence: Interior Minister Soylu reportedly opened an investigation into some police conduct, but the report gives no sign of effective remedy.

evidence.claim: The number of journalists held in Turkey rose from 18 in 2021 to 40 in 2022 after the arrests of 25 Kurdish journalists in the second half of the year, with lawyers saying the cases were driven by terrorism accusations tied to efforts to silence PKK-linked reporting.
evidence.title: Attacks on the Press in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The number of journalists held in Turkey rose from 18 in 2021 to 40 in 2022 after the arrests of 25 Kurdish journalists in the second half of the year, with lawyers saying the cases were driven by terrorism accusations tied to efforts to silence PKK-linked reporting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary CPJ annual census with a specific country count and explanation of the arrest wave.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Erdoğan because the arrests and custody occurred under his government's security and judicial apparatus.
contrary_evidence: CPJ counts custody, not sentence outcomes or every lower-level abuse case.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the new law tightened government grip over social media and news websites, could send people to prison for up to three years for a retweet, and created a chilling effect through fear of criminal prosecution.
evidence.title: Turkey: “Dark day for online free expression” as new ‘disinformation law’ is passed
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the new law tightened government grip over social media and news websites, could send people to prison for up to three years for a retweet, and created a chilling effect through fear of criminal prosecution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights criticism with the exact statutory penalty and a direct explanation of the likely chilling effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Erdoğan's governing coalition because it was enacted by parliament under his administration.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the law as an information-safety measure, not censorship.

evidence.claim: The Council of Europe said the draft criminal provision on false or misleading information interfered with freedom of expression and that there was no pressing social need to introduce it.
evidence.title: Türkiye - Draft criminal provision on “false or misleading information” interferes with freedom of expression says Venice Commission
evidence.excerpt: The Council of Europe said the draft criminal provision on false or misleading information interfered with freedom of expression and that there was no pressing social need to introduce it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Council of Europe press summary of the Venice Commission's urgent opinion; the direct page was available as a press release rather than the underlying PDF text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's government because the bill was part of the ruling-party legislative program.
contrary_evidence: This is a legal-opinion source; it evaluates the draft law rather than documenting every on-the-ground effect.

evidence.claim: A Turkish court jailed pop star Gülşen pending trial over a quip about religious schools; Reuters reported that critics said she was targeted for her support for LGBT+ rights and liberal views that clashed with Erdoğan's AK Party.
evidence.title: Turkish pop star to be moved to house arrest after detention sparked outrage
evidence.excerpt: A Turkish court jailed pop star Gülşen pending trial over a quip about religious schools; Reuters reported that critics said she was targeted for her support for LGBT+ rights and liberal views that clashed with Erdoğan's AK Party.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting with direct contemporaneous procedural facts and the political reaction around the case.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdoğan's political climate, though the formal arrest was a judicial act.
contrary_evidence: The court later moved her from jail to house arrest, so the state response was severe but not maximal.

evidence.claim: After the Istanbul bombing, Erdoğan called it a 'treacherous attack,' said its perpetrators would be punished, and said the initial information suggested terror involvement.
evidence.title: Istanbul blast: Kurdish groups deny involvement as Turkey detains dozens over 'terror attack'
evidence.excerpt: After the Istanbul bombing, Erdoğan called it a 'treacherous attack,' said its perpetrators would be punished, and said the initial information suggested terror involvement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire content mirrored by Euronews with clear attribution and direct quotations from Erdoğan.
contrary_evidence: The attack itself was real and deadly, so some strong rhetoric reflected genuine public-safety concern rather than pure incitement.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said a constitutional amendment would protect families from what he called 'perverse trends,' and the Reuters report described the remarks as appearing to target global same-sex marriage laws.
evidence.title: Erdoğan says constitutional amendment will protect families against 'perverse trends'
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said a constitutional amendment would protect families from what he called 'perverse trends,' and the Reuters report described the remarks as appearing to target global same-sex marriage laws.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reported on a direct Erdoğan speech and the political meaning of the remarks.
contrary_evidence: He also linked the proposal to headscarf rights, so the statement mixed a rights claim with stigmatizing language.

evidence.claim: The report states that same-sex relations are legal but there are no legal protections from discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and it cites reports of homophobic government rhetoric and public-morality provisions being used to restrict LGBT advocacy.
evidence.title: Türkiye: Treatment of persons with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC) by society and state authorities, including state protection (2020–November 2022)
evidence.publisher: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada
evidence.excerpt: The report states that same-sex relations are legal but there are no legal protections from discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and it cites reports of homophobic government rhetoric and public-morality provisions being used to restrict LGBT advocacy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent government research report that synthesizes cited sources and is explicit about legal gaps and state rhetoric.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Erdoğan because it describes state-level legal and rhetorical conditions during his rule.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some constitutional privacy protections and legal name/gender-change pathways for trans persons.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
